title: GPU memory headroom and dynamic budgeting for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
We need a robust, measurable approach to GPU memory budgeting that accounts for model weights, KV cache, activations, and operational headroom. This ticket proposes a dynamic budgeting model plus runtime controls that tie continuous batching and KV cache management to available headroom so we avoid OOMs, minimize conservative throttling, and maximize throughput.

Background and motivation:
- Recent canaries with 30B and 70B models exposed frequent conservative throttling: we reserve large static headrooms to avoid OOMs, which reduces throughput by 8–20% across mid-to-long sequence workloads.
- KV growth is workload-dependent (avg request length, chat history retention). Continuous batching exacerbates sudden KV spikes when long-context requests join a batch.
- Weights footprint varies by quantization profile (FP16/INT8/4-bit). Activations scale with sequence length and batch size. We must coordinate these three allocations at runtime.

Proposal (high level):
1) Deterministic memory model: compute an estimated memory demand per request as the sum of: weight_bytes (selected quantization profile) + kv_bytes (tokens * hidden_size * 2 * bytes_per_param) + transient_activation_bytes (estimated per-token activation multiplier * seq_length * batch_size). We will explicitly expose the formula in code and instrumentation.
2) Headroom policy: maintain a configurable headroom percentage and an absolute floor. Default: headroom_pct = 8%, headroom_abs = 512MB. Effective headroom = max(headroom_pct * gpu_total, headroom_abs).
3) Continuous batching integration: the batcher uses the memory model to compute the safe batch cap. The batcher will accept new requests only if estimated_batch_memory + reserved_headroom < available_free_memory. If unsafe, requests are queued or overflowed to a fallback model/region.
4) KV cache management: implement two complementary strategies: (a) soft-KV eviction policy that trims oldest prefixes when active memory pressure is observed, prioritized by per-customer TTL and pinned tokens; (b) adaptive per-session KV compression paths where we switch from FP16 to 8-bit stored KV (lossy) for long inactive sessions.
5) Telemetry and auto-tuning: collect per-GPU breakdown of weights/KV/activations/live_allocations and feed an auto-tuner that adjusts headroom_pct and batching thresholds per-instance class (GPU type + model family).

Tasks / Implementation plan:
- T1 (Marco): Implement deterministic memory estimator lib (C++) with unit tests and RPC to Python batcher. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 (WIP).
- T2 (Eileen): Add runtime metrics (weights_bytes, kv_bytes, activation_bytes, reserved_headroom, estimated_req_bytes) to per-request tracing and per-GPU summary. Grafana dashboards: /dashboards/gpu-memory-breakdown.
- T3 (Marco + SRE): Integrate estimator into continuous batcher flow. Enforce safe_batch_cap decisions and fallback policy.
- T4 (R&D: Anya): Prototype soft-KV eviction + compressed-KV store; benchmark LLAMA-30B chat workload. Experiment plan: 3 runs (baseline, soft-eviction, compressed-KV) with 1k warm sessions. Results will determine default policies.
- T5 (Ops): Canary rollout plan and rollback gates (OOM > 0.1% in 1h OR p95 latency regressions > 15%).

Acceptance criteria / Success metrics:
- End-to-end: production canary on a curated chat workload shows OOM rate < 0.05% and throughput within 5% of baseline (no headroom changes).
- Contention cases: when long-context spikes occur, the system should avoid global throttling and instead: a) soft-evict oldest unpinned KV segments for <= 2% of sessions, OR b) move those requests to fallback model with <10% quality degradation.
- Telemetry: per-GPU memory breakdown dashboards show accurate (within 7%) accounting vs. device-level allocator sampling.

Open trade-offs and risks:
- Soft-KV eviction risks degrading contextual quality for affected sessions; we will tie eviction to session importance and implement warning hooks so apps can rehydrate if needed.
- Compressed-KV reduces memory but can increase compute on de/compression path; need to measure tail latency.
- Aggressive auto-tuning could oscillate; we will add smoothing (exponential decay, 15-minute windows).

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1: run estimator + telemetry only in prod (read-only) for 2 weeks to validate modeling accuracy.
- Stage 2: enable safe_batch_cap enforcement on a small subset of instances (canary pool, 5%).
- Stage 3: enable soft-KV eviction and compressed-KV on canary with strict rollback gates.

Related links and artifacts:
- Design doc (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/GPU+Memory+Budgeting+Design
- PR (estimator core): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123 (WIP)
- Benchmarks (s3): s3://redwood-bench/gpu-memory/2026-03-kv-eviction-results.csv
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/gpu-memory-breakdown

Notes for reviewers:
- Focus review on the memory estimator assumptions (bytes per KV entry, activation multipliers) and the safety of soft-eviction policy.
- We need sign-off from SRE and Applied ML on fallback quality thresholds.
comments: 2026-03-06 - Eileen Park: Ran initial estimator calibration against 8 NV100 instances with LLAMA-30B. Observed model weights accounted for 86% of expected; activation estimator undercounts by ~12% for long prompts. Adjusted activation multiplier from 1.0 to 1.15 in calibration table.

2026-03-07 - Marco Chen: Pushed initial estimator PR (WIP). The unit tests include synthetic token sequences and compare against GPU allocator snapshots. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4123. Need perf review next.

2026-03-09 - Anya Singh (R&D): Soft-KV eviction prototype reduced max resident memory by ~6% on the 30B chat benchmark but increased p95 by 3% when eviction triggered. We should gate eviction to <=1 eviction/minute per-session by default.
2026-03-10 - SRE (L. Morales): Concern: headroom_pct=8% may be too tight for mixed workloads on older GPU generations. Recommend per-GPU-class defaults: A100:8%, V100:12%, T4:15%.
2026-03-11 - Marco Chen: Updated estimator to accept per-GPU-class headroom defaults and added smoothing to auto-tuner. Preparing canary config. Assigned T3 integration to me and SRE pair.

2026-03-12 - Product (Ravi Patel): Customer success flagged two enterprise customers requiring deterministic behavior for on-prem deployments; we must add a 'strict' mode that disables soft-eviction and falls back to queueing instead. Marking as requirement for release runtime-2.4.
